parsed.explanation: The large-prime erasure lemma (σ(x) good for every term x) is exactly ledger item L6.2 and carries the whole reduction to finitely many primes, hence L = product of p ≤ A. The write-up states it and replaces the proof with 'Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted).' No argument appears elsewhere: item 4 of 'Hypotheses tested' only names 'the construction Rp^k repairs this boundary issue' without defining R, k, or showing the resulting number is a term below x; the computational section explicitly says it 'only tests' the lemma. So L6.2 is unproved as written; supplying the omitted induction is a lemma-sized repair.
